evaluations.label: A
errors: 'Management decided against including teletext support or voice recognition' misattributes the voice-recognition decision. Management excluded teletext; the participants themselves argued against voice recognition on cost and necessity grounds.
The technical-interface summary associates potential LCD screens with the user interface designer. The marketing expert raised the LCD idea.

'Action Items (none)' is incorrect. Explicit next steps included questionnaires and summaries, role-specific individual work, uploading documentation and presentations, and the project manager resolving the missing presentation.
The notes introduce whether a lost-remote beep feature would fit the budget as an unresolved meeting question. That specific budget question was not discussed.
The charging cradle is described as improving 'location tracking.' It was proposed as a fixed storage location that might reduce loss, not as a tracking system.
strengths: Covers all three presentations and accurately preserves the major research percentages, button-use finding, and price constraints.
Captures television-only scope, teletext exclusion, corporate branding, and the simplicity-and-fashion priorities.
Generally distinguishes the unresolved target demographic and proposed charging cradle from settled requirements.
weaknesses: Omits the meeting's closing assignments and documentation responsibilities despite declaring that there were no actions.
The summary and outline repeat substantial material, making the notes longer without improving follow-through.
Unmapped speaker numbers make responsibilities and attributions harder to understand than the transcript's role labels.

evaluations.label: B
strengths: Faithfully distinguishes agreed priorities and functions from suggestions such as a sliding panel, charging cradle, and age-based targeting.
Accurately covers the research, presentations, scope restrictions, branding, prices, and feature trade-offs.
Correctly identifies the project manager's presentation as the missing file and records the manager's commitment to resolve it.
Clear topical organization and timestamp references make the notes easy to navigate and check.
weaknesses: The action-item list includes only two project-manager tasks; questionnaires and role-specific work appear in the body rather than as consolidated, owned actions.
Omits the marketing expert's conditional offer to email additional age data before the next meeting and the request that everyone upload their own slides.
Omits the 30-minute individual-work allocation and the instruction to record frustrations or issues in summaries. 'Speaker 1' is also less clear than 'Project Manager' as an action owner.

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'Target group 15–35 years' presents a tentative, voice-recognition-based suggestion as the target market. The team reconsidered it and did not settle on an age range.

'Provide updated market research data' is listed as an unconditional, unassigned action. The marketing expert only offered to email further age figures before the next meeting if additional data became available.
'Investigate technical feasibility for rechargeable battery' was not assigned. A rechargeable cradle was proposed and retained for consideration, without an explicit investigation task or owner.
strengths: Concise and easy to scan, with useful coverage of the main research percentages and frequently used controls.
Captures simplicity, fashion, prominent essential buttons, less-prominent advanced controls, and the loss-related function.
Correctly treats a rechargeable cradle as a possibility in the main notes and includes the living-room-space concern.
weaknesses: Misses the actual closing assignments: questionnaires and summaries, components and interface concepts, market-trend watching, and documentation uploads.
Omits important context including the €25 retail price, 100-person sample, corporate slogan, prototype-feedback proposal, and shared-folder problem.
Its action section substitutes speculative tasks for explicit assignments, while its target-market statement misleads the reader about an unresolved decision.

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'Target group: broad appeal, roughly under 65' gives an interim suggestion more finality than warranted. No age cutoff was settled.

'Agreed functions' specifies a button on the TV that makes the remote beep. That was an illustrative implementation; the agreement was to include a way to address remote loss, not that particular mechanism.

Listing a 'rechargeable or long-life battery solution' among agreed functions blurs the supported long-life-energy goal with the still-tentative rechargeable-cradle proposal. No power arrangement was selected.

'Working design presentation not yet on the server; save from email into shared folder' identifies the wrong presentation and turns a tentative workaround into an instruction. The industrial designer confirmed that the working-design presentation was uploaded; the missing file was the project manager's presentation, which the manager undertook to sort out.
strengths: Preserves the major market findings, retail and production prices, branding details, and television-only restrictions.
Includes the post-meeting questionnaire, summary, 30-minute individual-work period, role-specific workstreams, and forthcoming coach instructions.
Captures the conditional nature of sharing additional demographic data and explains why a cradle might reduce loss.
weaknesses: Overstates several tentative suggestions as settled specifications, especially the age boundary and locator implementation.
The incorrect upload instruction could send a reader to fix the wrong file; ownership of other follow-ups is also insufficiently explicit.
Omits the project manager's minutes/documentation commitment and important interface-design discussion about conventional layouts and prototype feedback.

rationale: Scores are equal-weight averages of the four criteria. B is the most faithful and actionable, particularly in separating decisions from proposals and identifying the missing file correctly. D covers substantial follow-through but contains a consequential file error and overstates tentative choices. A covers the design discussion well but incorrectly reports no actions and misses the closing assignments. C is concise but misstates the target market and replaces the actual assignments with unsupported or mischaracterized actions.
